shape_precedent: definition-poc/source-license-evidence.json — a claim, a pointer, the evidence in the source's own words, and a rule. This file is that shape one level down: it declares how a provider's own marks read, and what its licence permits on export.

defaults.reading: A provider with no declaration is not split. Its route text ships whole, exactly as the corpus sealed it. No declaration, no split.
defaults.export: A licence posture with no declaration is not exported. No licence is as absolute as a forbidding one.
defaults.closure: Once a provider is declared, its mark set is closed. A declared provider using a mark absent from its declaration is reported, and that row ships whole rather than being split under a rule that does not cover it.
defaults.naming: A posture's name is declared here, beside its export row, and nowhere else. A dual offer is named as a dual. No page re-derives a licence's name from the letters of its key; a posture this file does not declare is named by its key, verbatim — the visible cue that a declaration is missing.

no_derivatives.test: the posture carries a NoDerivatives term — the token 'nd' standing alone between separators, or the word 'noderivatives'
no_derivatives.rule: Refused. An export is a redistributed derivative of the reading; a NoDerivatives licence does not permit one.
no_derivatives.measured_2026_08_17: No NoDerivatives posture is present in the store today. The refusal is written before one arrives, because the admission rule in source-license-evidence.json admits any explicit Creative Commons posture and CC BY-ND is one.

undeclared_posture.test: the posture is absent from export_postures above
undeclared_posture.rule: Refused, and named in the export. A posture nobody has read is not a posture anybody may rely on.

no_posture.test: the M record carries no licence posture at all
no_posture.rule: Refused. Not having a licence is as absolute as having a forbidding one.

withholding.rule: A reading refused on licence is not silently dropped. The export names the word, says a reading was withheld, and gives the reason. A silent drop makes the record look like the reading never existed, which is a worse lie than the refusal.
withholding.hebrew: The Hebrew is the sealed text of the work and is governed by the work's own licence, not by the licence of any reading. Refusing a reading never removes a word from a Hebrew export.

wikisource_strongs_explicit_forms.label: Strong's Hebrew concordance with explicit source form lists
wikisource_strongs_explicit_forms.declared_from: The entry's own structure, read across all 20,670 routes: 20,533 definitions carry a colon and 19,142 of them (92.6%) have route text exactly equal to the text after it. Zero take the text before it.

:.means: separates the definition from the KJV rendering list

;.means: separates etymology from sense, and sense from sense, in the head

,.means: alternation — separates one rendering from the next

(.means: scope over the alternation: the group distributes across its head
(.evidence: bring (forth, in, into, to pass) is five renderings, not four fragments; 6,638 routes carry a comma inside the parentheses

-.means: attach at the stem, not concatenate: enter (…, -tering, -trance, -try) is entering, entrance, entry
-.rule: Not expanded. The attachment point is not derivable from the string, and joining naively produces 'enter-tering'. Rows carrying it ship their rendering list whole.

X.means: annotation on one item: the word appears only inside an idiom, never as a bare equivalent

+.means: annotation on one item: the word is supplied by the translators and is not in the Hebrew

unbalanced_parentheses.read_again: A closer that never opened and an opener that never closes are not the same failure, and refusing them the same way cost the reader every reading in the row.

closer_with_nothing_open.why: There is no scope. A ')' that opened nothing holds nothing inside it, so a comma standing outside every open parenthesis is dividing the route, not the inside of a group. The orphan character stays where the provider left it, inside whichever piece it fell in.
closer_with_nothing_open.evidence: beacon, X altogether, be(-come), accomplished, committed, like), break, cause, come (to pass), do, ... — one ')' too many after 'like'; every other parenthesis in the row balances, and the twenty renderings divide at the commas exactly as they do in the 20,444 rows that balance.
closer_with_nothing_open.falsifier: A row where the pieces do not rejoin, character for character, into the route they came from. That is checked on every row and refuses it whole.

opener_never_closed.rule: separate up to it; ship the rest whole
opener_never_closed.why: From an unclosed '(' onward the scope's extent is unknown, so a comma after it may be dividing the inside of a group the provider wrote. Nothing at or after that character is separated. What stands before it is untouched by the failure and separates normally.
opener_never_closed.evidence: --X be, keep in bondage, ... labour(-ing man, bring to pass, ... worshipper, — the '(' after 'labour' never closes and the row ends on a comma, so it is a truncation. Everything before 'labour(' is eleven whole renderings; everything from it is held as one.
opener_never_closed.falsifier: A row where a piece taken from before the unclosed opener still contains an unclosed opener of its own.

separates_on.declared_from: 17,005 of the 20,670 routes carry a comma, and 12,681 carry a parenthesis with 6,638 of those holding a comma inside it. The comma divides one English rendering from the next; the parenthesis is a scope the provider wrote, and a comma inside it is dividing the inside of that scope, not the route.
separates_on.rule: Separate on commas that stand outside every parenthesis. Every piece is kept. No piece is joined to another, no group is distributed across its head, no sigil is stripped: 'X be' stays 'X be' and 'bring (forth, in, into, to pass)' stays whole, because the provider wrote them that way.

refusals.unbalanced parentheses: the route ships whole — where a scope does not close, nothing can be said about what is inside it

head_mark.mark: one or two hyphens at the head of the route
head_mark.means: the tail of the separator that introduces the KJV rendering list
head_mark.declared_from: 264 routes begin with a hyphen. In 264 of 264 the route's own definition carries ':' immediately before the route text — the source writes ':--' to open the rendering list, and this ingest took the route as the text after the colon, carrying the dashes with it.
head_mark.rule: One or two hyphens at the head are part of that mark and the reading begins after them. Nothing is removed anywhere else in the route, and a hyphen inside the route is untouched.
head_mark.falsifier: A route beginning with a hyphen whose definition does not carry ':' immediately before it. Zero of 264 at the time of writing.

wikisource_strongs_explicit_forms.not_done_here: The definition is never mined for a reading. An earlier pass took the sense from before the colon and substituted it for the route the corpus emitted; that produced 10,849 readings no source ever emitted, and it is struck. Choosing a region of a record and putting it forward as the reading is a derivation, whatever it improves.

bolls_bdbt_brown_driver_briggs_hebrew_19.label: Bolls byte-pinned reformatted Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew 1906
bolls_bdbt_brown_driver_briggs_hebrew_19.declared_from: The entry's own structure: the route is a slice of the definition in 14,522 of 22,007 rows, and its parentheses carry binyan names rather than alternatives.

(.means: a binyan header — Qal, Niphal, Pual, Hiphil and the rest — standing over the glosses that follow it
(.evidence: (Qal) to go out, be extinguished — distributing this would manufacture 'Qal to go out', which no source attests

,.means: separates one gloss from the next within the binyan it stands under
,.note: Not expanded into separate readings in this pass. The binyan a gloss stands under is part of what the gloss means, and splitting without carrying the header forward would strip it.

bolls_bdbt_brown_driver_briggs_hebrew_19.not_declared_yet: Its parentheses carry binyan headers rather than scopes over an alternation, so a comma outside them is not obviously dividing one reading from the next. Until that is read from the source, nothing is separated and every route ships whole.

undeclared_note: The other 72 providers by source key are not declared. Their routes ship whole, which is what they do today, so nothing about them changes. The ranked order to work through is in synthesis/MARK-INVENTORY-2026-08-17.json: the top ten source keys cover 71.7% of all routes and the top eighteen cover 87.1%.

derivation.what_it_is: A route whose text is properly contained, at word boundaries, inside a sibling route standing on the same M and the same definition record. The provider wrote one sentence; the shorter route is a piece cut out of it, not a second thing the provider said.

measured_2026_08_17.worked example: R-000000 / M-Davidson-1855 on the key at shard 26 — two routes stand on one record: one is that record's whole sentence, the other a run cut out of it. The cut is marked as a cut and shown; it is not manufactured, and its missing half is not invented to balance the book. The forms themselves are not copied here: they are read from the store at that key.

derivation.the_boundary_is_the_licence: A fragment is a modification of the provider's record presented under the provider's name. Whether it may be presented at all is therefore not ours to decide from taste — it is what the provider's licence permits. So the boundary is set per provider by reading its licence, not by reading its punctuation.

by_posture.no_derivatives: Refused. A fragment is a derivative and a NoDerivatives licence does not permit one. The whole record stands in its place, as the provider wrote it.
by_posture.share_alike: Permitted, and marked. The reader is told the reading is a cut of the record below it rather than the record's own sentence, and the obligation travels with any export.
by_posture.attribution_only: Permitted, and marked. Attribution to a source for words it did not arrange that way is only honest if the arrangement is disclosed.
by_posture.public_domain: Permitted, and marked. The licence asks nothing, but the record is still not the provider's sentence and the page does not pretend it is.
by_posture.undeclared_or_absent: Refused, with the same reason as any undeclared posture: a permission nobody has read is not a permission.

derivation.what_is_never_done: A fragment is never completed. If a provider's sentence was cut and the other piece was dropped, that piece is not manufactured here to balance it — it was not attested, and inventing it would be worse than the asymmetry it fixes.

separation_is_not_derivation: A separation keeps every piece the mark divides and each piece is a run of the provider's own characters. A derivation keeps one piece and discards the rest, or joins pieces the provider never wrote together. This project does the first and never the second.
